 Edward Berger says Brad Pitt’s A24 film The Riders has completed filming
 Thursday, 5 November 2026, 13:13 
 Photo source: Variety 
 Brad Pitt stars as a father who sets out across Europe with his daughter to find his wife. 
 Speaking at the Evolution Mallorca International Film Festival, where he received this year’s Evolution Vision Award, director Edward Berger said filming had finished on The Riders, his upcoming A24 film starring Brad Pitt. Berger described it as a “singular perspective story told through the eyes of Brad Pitt.”
 This is reported by Variety .
 “It’s a story of a man who’s renovating a cottage in the ’80s, in Ireland, waiting for his daughter and wife to show up. Only the daughter shows up, and then they go on a European Odyssey to find [the wife.] [They go] to Greece, Brussels, Amsterdam… I won’t tell you what happens or if he finds her [laughs].” 
 – Edward Berger
 The film is adapted from Tim Winton’s novel of the same name. A24 financed it and will distribute it. David Kajganich, a frequent collaborator of Luca Guadagnino, wrote the screenplay. Producers include Scott Free, Berger’s Nine Hours, Pitt’s Plan B and Kajganich. Julianne Nicholson, Danny Huston, Camille Cottin, Michael Smiley and Lara Pulver are also in the cast.
 Advertisement 
 Berger also compared working with seven-year-old Coco Greenstone, who plays Pitt’s daughter, to filming Jack with 12-year-old Ivo Pietzcker. For Jack, Pietzcker filmed for six or eight weeks and needed a tutor. Berger said the city allowed six-hour shooting days with the child, instead of the usual five, and that he got the shot one minute before the six hours were up. “And we just made a film with another kid,” he said of The Riders. “It was the same thing. It’s like every day you just get it just before they take them.”
